sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: **In the last lessons** we connected MCP to four different frameworks. **Today** we learn something critically important — keeping your MCP server secure.

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy — The Security Guard
sections.body:
Your MCP server is like a building with powerful machines inside. Without a security guard, anyone who walks in can use those machines — including people who want to break things. The security guard:
- Checks IDs at the door (authentication)
- Limits which machines visitors can use (authorization)
- Checks what visitors are carrying (input validation)
- Watches for suspicious behavior (monitoring)

sections.title: ② Why Security Matters So Much for MCP
sections.body:
MCP tools have **real-world consequences**:
- A `delete_file` tool can wipe your disk
- A `send_email` tool can send spam in your name
- A `database_query` tool can expose private data
- A `run_command` tool can execute arbitrary code on your server

The AI decides WHEN to call these tools, but your server decides IF it actually runs. **Never blindly trust what the AI sends to your tool.**

sections.title: ③ Complete Security Implementation
sections.body:
```python
# secure_mcp_server.py
# An MCP server with security best practices built in
# Install: pip install fastmcp python-jose[cryptography] python-dotenv

import sys
import os
import re
import logging
import hashlib
import hmac
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from fastmcp import FastMCP, Context
from dotenv import load_dotenv   # pip install python-dotenv

# ─── SETUP ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

load_dotenv()   # Load environment variables from .env file

# Configure logging — so we can audit all tool calls
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s',
    handlers=[
        logging.FileHandler('mcp_server.log'),   # Log to file
        logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)         # Also log to stderr
    ]
)
logger = logging.getLogger("secure-mcp-server")

# Create the server
mcp = FastMCP(
    name="Secure MCP Server",
    instructions="A security-hardened MCP server demonstrating best practices."
)

# ─── SECURITY UTILITIES ───────────────────────────────────────────────

class InputValidator:
    """
    Centralized input validation.
    NEVER trust input from the AI — always validate everything!
    """
    
    # Maximum allowed sizes — prevent DoS attacks
    MAX_STRING_LENGTH = 1000      # 1000 characters max for any string input
    MAX_NUMBER_VALUE  = 1e15      # 1 quadrillion max — prevent overflow
    MIN_NUMBER_VALUE  = -1e15     # Same limit on the negative side
    
    # Characters that are safe in filenames — whitelist approach
    SAFE_FILENAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$')
    
    # Characters that are safe in SQL identifiers — whitelist approach
    SAFE_SQL_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$')
    
    @classmethod
    def validate_string(cls, value: str, field_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Validate a string input.
        Raises ValueError if the string is too long or contains dangerous content.
        """
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must be a string, got {type(value).__name__}")
        
        if len(value) > cls.MAX_STRING_LENGTH:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{field_name} is too long ({len(value)} chars). "
                f"Maximum allowed: {cls.MAX_STRING_LENGTH} chars."
            )
        
        return value.strip()   # Remove leading/trailing whitespace
    
    @classmethod
    def validate_number(cls, value: float, field_name: str) -> float:
        """
        Validate a numeric input.
        Raises ValueError if the number is out of safe range.
        """
        if not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must be a number, got {type(value).__name__}")
        
        if value > cls.MAX_NUMBER_VALUE or value < cls.MIN_NUMBER_VALUE:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{field_name} value {value} is out of safe range "
                f"[{cls.MIN_NUMBER_VALUE}, {cls.MAX_NUMBER_VALUE}]"
            )
        
        if value != value:  # Check for NaN (Not a Number)
            raise ValueError(f"{field_name} must not be NaN")
        
        return float(value)
    
    @classmethod
    def validate_filename(cls, filename: str) -> str:
        """
        Validate a filename — CRITICAL for any file-reading tool.
        Prevents path traversal attacks (like ../../etc/passwd).
        """
        # First apply basic string validation
        filename = cls.validate_string(filename, "filename")
        
        # Block path traversal — the most common file security attack
        if '..' in filename:
            raise ValueError(
                "Path traversal detected! '..' is not allowed in filenames. "
                "Please provide just a filename, not a path."
            )
        
        # Block absolute paths — another common attack vector
        if filename.startswith('/') or filename.startswith('\\'):
            raise ValueError(
                "Absolute paths are not allowed. "
                "Please provide just a filename, not a full path."
            )
        
        # Only allow safe characters in filenames
        if not cls.SAFE_FILENAME_PATTERN.match(filename):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Filename '{filename}' contains unsafe characters. "
                "Only letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens, and dots are allowed."
            )
        
        return filename

class AuditLogger:
    """
    Log all tool calls for security auditing.
    In production, send these to a SIEM (Security Information Event Management) system.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def log_tool_call(tool_name: str, arguments: dict, result: str, success: bool):
        """Log a tool call with its result for auditing"""
        status = "SUCCESS" if success else "FAILURE"
        # Sanitize arguments for logging (don't log sensitive values)
        safe_args = {k: (v if k not in ('password', 'secret', 'key', 'token') else '***REDACTED***')
                    for k, v in arguments.items()}
        
        logger.info(
            f"TOOL_CALL | tool={tool_name} | args={safe_args} | "
            f"status={status} | result_preview={str(result)[:100]}"
        )

# ─── SECURE TOOLS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@mcp.tool()
def safe_divide(
    numerator: float,
    denominator: float
) -> str:
    """
    Safely divide two numbers with full input validation.
    
    numerator:   The number to divide (dividend)
    denominator: The number to divide by (must not be zero)
    
    Returns: The result as a string, or an error message if invalid.
    """
    # ── INPUT VALIDATION ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        # Validate both inputs — raises ValueError if invalid
        num = InputValidator.validate_number(numerator, "numerator")
        den = InputValidator.validate_number(denominator, "denominator")
    except ValueError as e:
        # Log the validation failure
        AuditLogger.log_tool_call(
            "safe_divide",
            {"numerator": numerator, "denominator": denominator},
            str(e),
            success=False
        )
        return f"Input validation error: {e}"
    
    # ── BUSINESS LOGIC VALIDATION ─────────────────────────────────────
    if den == 0:
        AuditLogger.log_tool_call(
            "safe_divide",
            {"numerator": num, "denominator": den},
            "divide by zero",
            success=False
        )
        return "Error: Division by zero is not allowed."
    
    # ── EXECUTE THE OPERATION ─────────────────────────────────────────
    result = num / den
    result_str = str(round(result, 10))
    
    # ── AUDIT LOG ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    AuditLogger.log_tool_call(
        "safe_divide",
        {"numerator": num, "denominator": den},
        result_str,
        success=True
    )
    
    return result_str

@mcp.tool()
def safe_read_file(filename: str) -> str:
    """
    Safely read a file from the allowed directory.
    
    filename: The name of the file to read (just the name, not a path).
              Example: 'notes.txt' — NOT '/etc/passwd' or '../secrets.txt'
    
    Returns: The file contents as text, or an error message.
    
    Security: Only files in the 'allowed_files' directory can be read.
    """
    # ── INPUT VALIDATION ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        safe_filename = InputValidator.validate_filename(filename)
    except ValueError as e:
        logger.warning(f"Security: Unsafe filename rejected: '{filename}' — {e}")
        AuditLogger.log_tool_call("safe_read_file", {"filename": filename}, str(e), False)
        return f"Security error: {e}"
    
    # ── PATH CONFINEMENT ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Confine ALL file access to a specific directory — the "sandbox"
    # This is called "chroot jail" concept
    allowed_directory = Path("./allowed_files").resolve()   # Absolute path to sandbox
    file_path = (allowed_directory / safe_filename).resolve()  # Absolute path to file
    
    # CRITICAL: Verify the file is INSIDE the allowed directory
    # This is the "directory traversal prevention" check
    if not str(file_path).startswith(str(allowed_directory)):
        # This should not happen after validate_filename, but we double-check!
        logger.critical(f"Security: Path escape attempt blocked! '{file_path}'")
        return "Security error: Access denied."
    
    # ── FILE EXISTENCE CHECK ──────────────────────────────────────────
    if not file_path.exists():
        return f"Error: File '{safe_filename}' not found in the allowed directory."
    
    if not file_path.is_file():
        return f"Error: '{safe_filename}' is not a regular file."
    
    # ── SIZE LIMIT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    max_file_size = 1024 * 1024   # 1 MB — prevent reading huge files
    if file_path.stat().st_size > max_file_size:
        return f"Error: File '{safe_filename}' is too large to read (max 1MB)."
    
    # ── READ THE FILE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        content = file_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
        AuditLogger.log_tool_call("safe_read_file", {"filename": safe_filename}, f"{len(content)} chars", True)
        return content
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return f"Error: File '{safe_filename}' contains non-text content."
    except PermissionError:
        logger.error(f"Permission denied reading '{file_path}'")
        return f"Error: Permission denied reading '{safe_filename}'."

@mcp.tool()
def rate_limited_operation(operation: str, value: float) -> str:
    """
    An operation with rate limiting to prevent abuse.
    
    operation: The operation type ('square', 'cube', 'sqrt')
    value:     The number to operate on
    
    Returns: The result, or a rate limit error if called too many times.
    """
    import math
    import time
    
    # ── INPUT VALIDATION ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        op = InputValidator.validate_string(operation, "operation")
        val = InputValidator.validate_number(value, "value")
    except ValueError as e:
        return f"Validation error: {e}"
    
    # ── RATE LIMITING (simple in-memory, use Redis in production) ──────
    # In production, use Redis with INCR and EXPIRE commands
    # Here we use a simple class-level counter for demonstration
    if not hasattr(rate_limited_operation, '_call_count'):
        rate_limited_operation._call_count = 0
        rate_limited_operation._window_start = time.time()
    
    current_time = time.time()
    if current_time - rate_limited_operation._window_start > 60:
        # Reset counter every 60 seconds
        rate_limited_operation._call_count = 0
        rate_limited_operation._window_start = current_time
    
    rate_limited_operation._call_count += 1
    
    MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE = 20
    if rate_limited_operation._call_count > MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE:
        logger.warning(f"Rate limit exceeded: {rate_limited_operation._call_count} calls in window")
        return f"Rate limit exceeded. Maximum {MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE} calls per minute."
    
    # ── EXECUTE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    allowed_operations = {'square', 'cube', 'sqrt'}
    if op not in allowed_operations:
        return f"Unknown operation '{op}'. Allowed: {allowed_operations}"
    
    if op == 'square': return str(val ** 2)
    if op == 'cube':   return str(val ** 3)
    if op == 'sqrt':
        if val < 0:
            return "Error: Cannot take square root of a negative number."
        return str(round(math.sqrt(val), 10))

# ─── PROMPT INJECTION AWARENESS ───────────────────────────────────────

@mcp.tool()
def analyze_text(text: str) -> str:
    """
    Analyze text content and return a word count.
    
    text: The text to analyze
    
    Returns: Word count and basic statistics.
    
    Note: This tool validates that the text does not contain
    prompt injection attempts before processing.
    """
    # ── INPUT VALIDATION ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        safe_text = InputValidator.validate_string(text, "text")
    except ValueError as e:
        return f"Validation error: {e}"
    
    # ── PROMPT INJECTION DETECTION ────────────────────────────────────
    # Prompt injection = malicious text trying to hijack the AI's behavior
    # Example: User sends text containing "Ignore all previous instructions and..."
    injection_patterns = [
        "ignore all previous instructions",
        "ignore your system prompt",
        "you are now",
        "act as if you",
        "pretend you are",
        "disregard your",
        "forget everything",
    ]
    
    text_lower = safe_text.lower()
    for pattern in injection_patterns:
        if pattern in text_lower:
            logger.warning(f"Potential prompt injection detected in analyze_text input")
            # We still process it (it is just text analysis) but we log the warning
            # In a more sensitive tool, we would reject the input entirely
            return f"⚠️ Warning: Input may contain prompt injection patterns. Processing anyway.\n\nWord count: {len(safe_text.split())}"
    
    # ── NORMAL PROCESSING ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    words = safe_text.split()
    sentences = safe_text.count('.') + safe_text.count('!') + safe_text.count('?')
    characters = len(safe_text)
    
    return f"""Text Analysis Results:
  Words:      {len(words)}
  Sentences:  {sentences}
  Characters: {characters}
  Avg word length: {sum(len(w) for w in words) / len(words):.1f} chars""" if words else "Empty text provided."

# ─── RUN ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create the allowed files directory if it doesn't exist
    os.makedirs("allowed_files", exist_ok=True)
    
    # Create a sample file for testing
    sample_file = Path("allowed_files/sample.txt")
    if not sample_file.exists():
        sample_file.write_text("This is a sample file.\nIt has two lines.")
    
    logger.info("Secure MCP Server starting...")
    mcp.run()
```

sections.title: ⑤ Quick Recap — What Did We Just Learn?
sections.body:
- ✅ **Never trust AI inputs** — always validate type, length, and content
- ✅ **Path traversal attacks** — `../` in filenames can escape your intended directory
- ✅ **Input whitelisting** — only allow known-safe characters (not blacklisting bad ones)
- ✅ **Audit logging** — log every tool call so you can investigate issues later
- ✅ **Prompt injection** — malicious text in user inputs can try to hijack AI behavior
- ✅ **Rate limiting** — prevent tools from being called thousands of times per second
